notes: ICRP 72 value; includes thyroid committed dose; 50-year committed effective dose; updated ICRP 158 (2024) gives 1.6E-08 (-27% revised biokinetic model); used for dose assessments of 1986 USSR populations

~5.5x adult effective dose coefficient; smaller thyroid mass (1.2g vs 16g adult) means same Bq delivers proportionally higher thyroid dose; higher fractional GI absorption; critical for explaining child-vs-adult thyroid cancer disparity
~2.4x adult value; intermediate between infant and adult; significant age-dependence over childhood

Thyroid equivalent dose coefficient >> effective dose because weighting factor wT(thyroid)=0.04; thyroid receives 4.3E-07 Sv/Bq = >10x effective dose coefficient; explains why thyroid is the critical organ for I-131

Infant thyroid dose coefficient = 2.4E-06 Sv/Bq = 5.6x adult thyroid coefficient; basis for high thyroid doses in pre-school evacuees (26% received >5 Gy thyroid per UNSCEAR); KI most effective if given to young children

Inhalation of radioiodine vapor; Type F = fast lung absorption; I-131 mainly vapor (>50%) in ambient air; inhalation adds to ingestion dose but milk pathway dominated in 1986 accident; firefighters at Chernobyl received significant inhalation doses
Infant inhalation coefficient; 4x adult; children breathe more air per kg body weight AND have smaller thyroid mass; both factors increase dose

External dose from deposited I-131 negligible compared to internal dose via milk/food; 364 keV gamma penetrating but physical decay (t1/2=8d) reduces exposure quickly; more relevant for workers in contaminated areas first weeks

Widely used value; ICRP 72; 50-year committed effective dose; Cs distributed in muscle tissue like K; biological half-life 70-140 days in adults (shorter in children); updated ICRP 158 gives 1.4E-08 (+8% minor revision)

~3.4x adult value; shorter biological retention time in children partially offsets higher dose rate per Bq; diet higher in specific foods (mushrooms less relevant for young children); body burden Cs-137 dominated this age group in contaminated Belarus schools

Lower than ingestion coefficient for Cs-137 because same Bq inhaled distributes to same tissues as ingested but with different GI absorption dynamics; Type M = moderate lung dissolution rate; key for liquidators inhaling contaminated dust

Sv per second per Bq/m2 on ground; Ba-137m 662 keV gamma (85.1% yield) from secular equilibrium with Cs-137 is the external dose source; this coefficient used for dose rate mapping from soil deposition data; 2026 CEZ dose rates derived from this

µGy/hr per MBq at 1 meter; specific gamma dose rate constant Γ=8.64 nGy m2 MBq-1 h-1; used to convert MBq/m2 soil to ambient dose rate; Prypiat 4.932 µSv/h corresponds to ~1.5-2 MBq/m2 residual Cs-137 assuming equilibrium
source: Health Physics dose rate constants; IAEA DS379

notes: 50-year committed effective dose; bone surface dose dominant (Sr is Ca-mimetic → bone seeker); bone surface wT=0.01; ICRP 72 value; updated ICRP 158 gives 2.4E-08 (-14% revised strontium biokinetics); Sr-90 dose higher than Cs-137 per Bq due to bone retention

Bone surface committed equivalent dose coefficient >> effective dose because bone surface receives very high local dose from Sr-90 beta (0.546 MeV) and Y-90 daughter (2.28 MeV beta); bone surface wT=0.01 used in effective dose

~8x adult value; infants have much higher bone remodeling and Ca/Sr uptake rates; growing bone accumulates Sr-90 more efficiently; breast-fed infants received highest Sr-90 bone doses when mothers consumed contaminated milk 1986-1988
Comparable to ingestion; both routes result in Sr-90 bone uptake; inhalation Type M = moderate lung transfer to blood; important for liquidators working in dust-contaminated areas near reactor

Higher than Cs-137 (1.3E-08) per Bq because Cs-134 has multiple high-energy gammas (605+796 keV) contributing to whole-body dose in addition to beta; important in first 5 years post-accident when Cs-134 still significant

Pu oxide or hydroxide form; f1=0.00001 (very low GI absorption); despite tiny GI absorption fraction the dose coefficient high because absorbed Pu goes to bone and liver permanently; ICRP dose coefficient reflects 50-year commitment from bone

MUCH higher than ingestion because inhalation deposits Pu in lung directly; lung committed dose plus systemic dose from lung transfer; Type M = 10% lung absorption rate; main concern for near-zone soil disturbance; Chernobyl Pu-239 released 0.030 PBq

Slightly lower than Pu-239 effective dose coefficient per Bq; however specific activity of Pu-238 is ~280x higher than Pu-239 per gram (shorter t1/2) so same mass gives 280x more activity → more dose per gram

Highest of commonly discussed actinides per Bq via inhalation; Chernobyl Pu-238 released 0.035 PBq; hot particles containing Pu-238 in near-zone represent primary inhalation dose for future CEZ workers

Slightly lower than Pu-239; Am-241 has higher solubility fraction from GI tract than Pu; also goes to bone and liver; current Am-241 activity in CEZ soils still growing (ingrowth from Pu-241); am241_ingrowth_timeseries_REAL.csv

Comparable to Pu-238 inhalation; high inhalation dose coefficient; Am-241 in surface soils of near-zone increasingly important as concentration grows toward 2058.7 peak; 59.5 keV gamma allows aerial and ground survey detection

Much lower than Cs or Sr per Bq; large intestine and bone surface are target tissues; biological half-time in GI ~2-4 days; Ru does not bioaccumulate strongly; 73 PBq released 1986 but mostly decayed by 1990; 2017 Ru-106 event: European population dose negligible
Higher than ingestion due to lung dose; some species of Ru are very soluble (Ru oxide/hydroxide); 2017 European event estimated max individual dose <0.1 mSv even in Romania at detection maximum

Te-132 parent of I-132; 1150 PBq released; short-lived; ingested Te-132 converts to I-132 in thyroid; combined Te-132+I-132 dose pathway relevant in first days post-accident; Te-132 GI conversion to I-132 adds to direct I-131 thyroid dose
Sr-89 t1/2=50.5 days; 115 PBq released; short-lived bone dose contributor; only relevant 1986-1988; decayed to negligible by 1990; bone dose in first year was significant addition to Sr-90 bone dose

Ba-140 t1/2=12.75 days; 240 PBq released; parent of La-140 (t1/2=40hr); Ba-140/La-140 secular equilibrium; bone-seeker (like Sr but less avidly); decayed within 6 months; relevant only for immediate 1986 dose near plant

Very low dose coefficient because noble gas Xe-133 does not fix in tissues; passes through body rapidly; but 6500 PBq released and spread globally; external exposure (cloud shine/ground shine) more significant than internal; gave radiation sickness symptoms to people in plume

Low dose coefficient because Pu-241 is primarily beta emitter (0.021 MeV) with no alpha; 2.6 PBq released; health significance mainly through ingrowth to Am-241 (not via Pu-241 dose itself); 50-year commitment minor; 100-year commitment via Am-241 daughter is significant

Children 10yr receive 2.1x adult effective dose per Bq Cs-137 ingested; combined with children's higher consumption of fresh foods → explains higher Cs-137 body burdens in children (cs137_body_burden_ukraine_REAL.csv: teenagers highest group)

KI tablet (stable iodine) given within 2 hours of exposure blocks thyroid I-131 uptake by >90%; effectiveness decreases rapidly after exposure: 50% blockade if given 6h late; <10% if given 24h late; only Poland in USSR bloc distributed KI — explains dramatically lower Polish thyroid cancer rates

Approximate effective dose rate (µSv/hr) per kBq/m2 of Cs-137 in soil; used for dose rate → deposition conversion; Prypiat ~1145 kBq/m2 Cs-137 in 1986 → 4.9 µSv/hr now consistent with SaveEcoBot readings; geometric mean for standard soil buildup factor
